items.title: Conrad "Connie" Jones Interview, 1981-09-01
items.q: I never did call Jack Teagarden anything but Mr. Teagarden... But to me, you just didn't speak to a deity on a first name basis.

ctx.x: Anyone who was older than you was Mr. and if you grew up with them, I would have been a little bit more. And if you grew up with them, it was still Mr. if somebody was 15 years older than you. It was hard making the transition from Mr. Allen to Dick or Richard. Because it just became a habit. Someone was Mr. So and so. And I never did call Jack Teagarden anything but Mr. Teagarden. Now Addie was different, because everybody called her Addie, Mrs. Tebow. But to me, you just didn't speak to a deity on a first name…
Who did call him Jack? Everybody. Excuse me, everybody. The first time they ever met him they called him Jack? I don't know.
Yeah, I guess so. Yeah, I think so.

items.title: Conrad "Connie" Jones Interview, 1981-07-23, 08-03
items.q: It was a club that I worked with when I was a kid. with Jack Teagarden, that's where Jack died.

ctx.x: Yeah, that's how I remember it. Don't think I heard it too much. Where was your blank puppet again?
I first joined them at the Club Slipper on Bourbon Street, which is the 400 block. It was a club that I worked with when I was a kid.
with Jack Teagarden, that's where Jack died. You familiar with the location? It's a plaque out on the wall there now, monstrous plaque, it must be every bit this big. And then we uh...
